newsitem.title: USA: Gilat to acquire Skydata, post Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Gilat to acquire Skydata, post Q4 charge.

text.p: Gilat Satellite Networks Ltd said on Thursday it has acquired Skydata Inc through an exchange of all outstanding equity of Skydata for about eight percent of Gilat ordinary shares.
Gilat said it expects the anticipated merger and restructuring costs to be $2 million and $4 million, respectively. These charges will be posted in the company's fourth quarter results.
Skydata is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Gilat and the acquisition will be accounted for as a pooling of interest, the Tel Aviv-based company said.
The major investors and marketing partners of Skydata are Korea's Samsung Co and Europe's Matra Marconi Space France SA which, as a result of the acquisition, have become shareholders of Gilat.

"The acquisition offers Gilat an additional U.S. base of operations to help support our customers and marketing efforts in the United States. We also intend to use the Florida location as a springboard to Latin America," said Yoel Gat, Gilat's chairman and chief executive.
Skydata President John Todd will report to Gilat's president and chief operating officer, Amiram Levinberg, the company said.
